 Crl.P No. 2600 of 2024
 This Crl.P Is Filed U/S.439 Of Cr.P.C Praying To
Enlarge Accused No.1 / Petitioner On Anticipatory
Bail In The Event Of Arrest, On His Appearance Before
Concerned Jurisdictional Court In Connection With
The Case In C.C.No.599/2011 Or C.C.No.349/2024, For The
Offence P/U/S 354, 506, 384, 509, 376 And 511 And 120(B)
R/W Sec. 34 Of Ipc, On The File Of The Addl.

Civil Judge
And Jmfc, Ramanagara.

This Petition, Coming On For Orders, This Day,
The Court Made The Following:
 Order

The petitioner-accused No.1 is before this Court seeking grant of anticipatory bail in the event of his arrest on his appearance before jurisdictional court in connection with C.C.No.599/2011 or C.C.No.349/2024 registered for the offences punishable under Sections 354, 506, 384, 509, 376 and 511 and 120(B) read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code, 1860 (for short 'IPC').
2.

Heard Sri.Ashwin Vaish, learned counsel for Sri.Vinay Kutlappa, learned counsel for the petitioner and Sri.Rahul Rai K., learned High Court Government Pleader for NC: 2024:KHC:20285 the respondent No.1-State and Sri.E.R.Gajendra Naidu, learned counsel for respondent No.2.
Perused the materials on record.
3.

In view of the rival contentions urged by the learned counsel for both the parties, the point that would arise for my consideration is:
"Whether the petitioner is entitled for grant of bail under Section 438 of Cr.P.C.?"

My answer to the above point is in 'Affirmative' for the following:
REASONS 4.
The petitioner - accused No.1 is seeking grant of anticipatory bail on the apprehension of being arrested.
A private complaint was filed by the complainant making allegations against accused Nos.1 to 3 for the offences punishable under Sections 376, 354, 384, 506, 509 r/w Section 34 of IPC.

Later,
an order was passed dropping Section 376 of IPC.

It was challenged by the complainant by filing a criminal petition before this court, which came to be allowed and the order of the learned Magistrate was modified by invoking NC: 2024:KHC:20285 Section 376 of IPC.
In the meantime, the summons issued against accused No.1 was challenged by him by filing a revision and the same came to be dismissed.

When a petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C was preferred before this court, the same Sri. Nithya Dharmananda @ K. Lenin vs The State Of Karnataka on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/23258715/
2 was rejected.

entities.text: Nithya Dharmananda @ K. Lenin vs The State Of Karnataka on 11 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even the SLP preferred came to be dismissed.
Thus, the fact remains that Section 376 of IPC was invoked as per the order of this court in Criminal Petition No.763/2011.

In the meantime,
petitioner is said to have obtained bail, when Section 376 of IPC was already dropped.
After allowing the criminal petition by invoking Section 376 IPC, it is the contention of the petitioner that he was appearing before the committal court on various dates of hearing.
The said submission is supported by the documents produced before this court.
It is to be noted that now the petitioner had applied for grant of anticipatory bail.

It is stated that now the petitioner apprehends arrest in view of the order dated 27.01.2024 passed by the learned Magistrate once again taking cognizance for the offence punishable under Section 376 of IPC.
Therefore, on 06.02.2024, he moved the learned Sessions Judge for grant of anticipatory bail, which came to be rejected.
Therefore, the petitioner is before this court.
Considering the facts stated above, it is undisputed that when the petitioners sought of anticipatory bail, Section 376 of IPC was not invoked.
It was invoked later and the court has taken cognizance of the same.
Under such circumstances, it cannot be said that the petition is not maintainable.

6. The learned counsel for the petitioner has placed reliance on the decision in BHADRESH BIPINBHAI SHETH VS. STATE OF GUJARAT1 in support of his contention, wherein the Hon'ble Apex Court has categorically held that once the accused is released on anticipatory bail by the trial court, then it would be unreasonable to compel the accused to surrender before the trial court once again and once again apply for regular bail.

entities.text: BHADRESH BIPINBHAI SHETH VS. STATE OF GUJARAT1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The learned counsel has also relied on decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in SUSHILA AGGARWAL VS. STATE (NCT OF DELHI)2, wherein, the Constitution bench of the Hon'ble Apex Court referred to the decision in 'BHADRESH BIPINBHAI SHETH (supra) and reiterated the principle laid down by the court.

entities.text: SUSHILA AGGARWAL VS. STATE (NCT OF DELHI)2,
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
Thus, when once the petitioner is already granted anticipatory bail when Section 376 of IPC (2016) 1 SCC 152 (2020) 5 SCC 1 NC:
2024:KHC:20285 was not invoked, there is no impediment for the petitioner to seek anticipatory bail for the offence punishable under section 376 of IPC.
Therefore, I am the opinion that the petition is maintainable.
6. On facts, a private complaint was registered by the complainant against accused Nos.1 to 3.

Much prior to filing of the private complaint by the complainant, it is the contention of the petitioner that he had filed the first information, which was registered in Crime No.141/2010 of Ramanagara Police Station against the accused who is said to be the spiritual guru of the present complainant.

It is not the contention of the complainant or the prosecution that the petitioner is required once again for investigation or for any other purpose except to ensure his presence before the trial court.
Admittedly, the matter before the learned Magistrate is for passing the order for committal.
Under such circumstances, I do not find any reason to reject the claim of the petitioner for grant of anticipatory bail.

7. Accordingly, I answer the above point in the affirmative and proceed to pass the following:

sentences.text: The petition is allowed.

The petitioner is ordered to be enlarged on bail in the event of his arrest on his appearance before jurisdictional court in connection with C.C.No.599/2011 or C.C.No.349/2024 registered for the offences punishable under Sections 354, 506,
384, 509, 376 and 511 and 120(B) read with Section 34 of Indian Penal Code, 1860.

The petitioner is directed to appear before the Investigating Officer within 15 days from the date of receipt of this order and on his appearance, the Investigating Officer shall enlarge him on bail subject to the following conditions:-
a.

The petitioner shall furnish the bond in a sum of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lakhs only) with two sureties for the likesum to the satisfaction of the Investigating Officer;
b.

The petitioner shall not commit similar offences;
c.
The petitioner shall appear before the Investigating Officer or the court as and when required; and NC: 2024:KHC:20285 d.
The petitioner shall not threaten or tamper the prosecution witnesses.
On furnishing the sureties by the petitioner, the Investigating Officer is at liberty to verify the correctness of the address and authenticity of the documents furnished by him.
On satisfaction of the said documents, he may proceed to accept the sureties within a reasonable time.
In view of the disposal of the petition, all pending I.As stand disposed of.
